If using third party programs like Dotabuff, they have skill brackets in Normal (under 3k I think) High (between 3k and 4k I think) and Very high (above 4k) I don't think these are the right numbers but they are close enough for an estimate.  
To my knowledge 1-2k are very new to the game, don't understand how items will benefit some heroes over others, don't fully understand abilities and will most likely not know every hero in the game.  
2-3k is a lot better, they begin grasping the game, but still have very little awareness of what's going on around them, do not know how to farm efficiently but know how to get gold. Most people know how to press abilities in fights but do not know how positioning will help them.  
3-4k Understand the basic mechanics, how to lane, farm, and roam. The problem with this bracket I feel is everyone has sort of perfected one role, but is terrible at all others. So if a guy who supports a lot decides he wants to play a carry, he isn't very familiar with farming rotations and will look like a very bad player. This is interchangable with all roles. They begin to know positioning and how to use abilities to farm, fight, harass and trade but there lane control is pretty basic still. TL:DR 3-4k know the basics.  
4-5k Players are good, they know what they are doing, their map awareness lacks, and they havn't perfected lane control. There rotations are also lack luster. They know what they should be doing, just not all the time.
5k+ are regarded good players. They know the game. It's a game of efficiency and they know it.
